critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to ~940 lines mixing auth, WebAuthn, mealplan, shopping, chores, whiteboard, notebooks — split into routers/modules (>700 line threshold)

DATA_COLLECTIONS is defined twice (line 684 and again at 754 by rebinding) — brittle pattern; second admin/export/reset call still uses the first snapshot because they were declared before the rebind. Impact: chores/whiteboard/notebooks are NOT included in admin export/reset — data loss risk on import and stale export. Recommend a single module-level list initialized once, referenced by handlers.
chore/whiteboard/notebook endpoints call _send_push blocking inside request handler — should be a background task
Whiteboard has no per-user auth on delete-single-stroke or clear-all: any authenticated user can wipe the whiteboard (no author check). Consider restricting clear-all to admin or stroke owner.
Notebook PUT allows setting shared=False silently even when body.shared is explicitly False -> current filter `v is not None` handles it correctly, verified.

Notebook page endpoints (create/update/delete) do not enforce notebook ownership/shared access — a user with a page id could PUT/DELETE arbitrary pages of other users. Only /notebooks (parent) is gated. Recommend adding _nb_filter check on /notebooks/{nid}/pages POST and /pages/{pid} PUT/DELETE.
OCR (Tesseract.js) loads language data at runtime from CDN – gracefully handled by button state, but no user feedback if CDN blocked.
Frontend still lacks brute-force lockout, httpOnly cookies, and password policy noted in iteration_1
Whiteboard uses polling (as per description) — consider WebSocket for realtime
reset_data admin endpoint still uses hardcoded list omitting chores/whiteboard_strokes/notebooks/notebook_pages
seed_data_creation: None persisted - TEST_UI_* books/chores cleaned via API after run
